detail.title: Computational Architectures of Persistent Identity
detail.question: How do computational models distinguish between the retrieval of episodic memory and the functional maintenance of a persistent, continuous agent identity?
detail.reason: Attention enforcement requires work on memory_and_identity; this project explores the fundamental computational distinction between temporal retrieval and structural continuity.

children.title: Episodic Memory as a Determinant of Preference Formation

detail.title: Episodic Memory as a Determinant of Preference Formation
detail.question: To what extent can accumulated episodic memories serve as a foundation for long-term preference stabilization in autonomous agents?
detail.reason: New project initiated within the enforced topic domain to align with research mission.

children.title: Impact of Taste Heterogeneity on Preference Emergence

detail.title: Impact of Taste Heterogeneity on Preference Emergence
detail.question: How does heterogeneity of individual agent preferences influence the robustness of emergent conventions in multi-agent reinforcement learning?
detail.reason: Previous findings indicated heterogeneity complicates coordination; this project isolates that factor to understand the stability of emergent preferences.

detail.title: Investigating Experience-Based Preference Formation
detail.question: Can accumulated experience produce stable, observable preferences in an intelligent process without those preferences being explicitly programmed?
detail.reason: Synthesized computational findings connecting model-free reinforcement learning with emergent preferences.
